answer: A vault only counts what it can prove it stored. Each identity must deposit shale receipts from two distinct holders outside its own seam, and one receipt cannot back two identities, so relaying it merges the claims into one seat. Storage is priced by depth: the k-th receipt an operator banks costs k squared in bond, so n aliases pay near n cubed while still needing n unrelated depositors. Every epoch a random audit asks for the original nectar ticket behind a receipt; a receipt traced to a shared funder voids the whole seam, and receipts cannot be sold or re-dated.
